slides.title: Start with intended use
bullets: Tell us the dose, route and available administration volume.
Distinguish exposure preparation from a product intended for storage.
Identify dilution medium and any constraints on excipient loading.

rows: Assess whether dosing uses comparable material

slides.title: Vehicle ladder workflow
bullets: Agree target concentration in mg/mL before choosing recipes.
Prepare candidate vehicles and capture preparation behavior on bench sheets.
Compare standing and dilution observations alongside initial appearance.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Appearance does not establish dose suitability
bullets: A clear concentrate may precipitate when diluted.
A suspension may settle yet remain usable if it redisperses reliably.
The selected route must match the intended withdrawal and handling steps.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Dose loading: explicit tradeoffs
bullets: Higher concentration can reduce required dose volume.
Increasing excipient weight percent can improve solvent support.
bullets_right: Viscosity and mixing can limit preparation and withdrawal.
Dilution can remove the support that made the concentrate attractive.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Excipient compatibility screen
bullets: Define the excipient combinations and comparison conditions.
Capture appearance and relevant compatibility observations.
Use the result to prioritize follow-up; do not infer shelf-life from a short screen.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Screen suitability and interpretation

rows: Comparisons must refer to the intended preparation
A changed order can change behavior
Claims apply to the examined condition
Retain failures beside the preferred route

slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Particle size and suspension handling
bullets: Describe measured particle sizes in µm.
Consider wetting, settling, caking and recovery together.
A finer distribution is useful only when the resulting preparation remains workable.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Manufacturability questions before expansion
bullets: Can the addition order and mixing method be reproduced?
Does the container permit recovery of settled material?
What material demand follows from preparation losses and repeat needs?
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Pilot-lot preparation is a new scale gate
bullets: Agree preparation volume, equipment class and hold interval.
Carry forward the screen rationale, not only the selected excipient list.
Document differences from the exploratory recipe before treating output as comparable.
slides.footer: Durnesswick Laboratories Inc, a Tarnovell company | Confidential

slides.title: Scope and capability boundaries
bullets: Exploratory screening supports a next-step decision.
A locked process requires evidence of reproducibility under defined controls.
Shelf-life, dose uniformity and larger-scale performance must be scoped when required.
